records.subagent_summary: With the incumbent hint 1/8 rollouts scored 1 (execution 149.178) and 7 of 8 hit finish_reason=length at the 16384-token cap, so the dominant failure is non-termination, not a missing concept: the failures re-derived 'but the speaker could just subtract/divide, so this case is impossible', restarted the same two-case enumeration many times, and either ran out of tokens or gave up and boxed a plausible factor. The revision states outright that a speaker's own value pinning the partner under one fixed option is not a contradiction, converts 'I don't know' into a reusable condition on the speaker's value that later speakers intersect, and asks for one symbolic forward pass with an explicit ban on restarting, which targets the loop that consumed seven rollouts.

7 of 8 round-9 rollouts scored 1; the single failure took the 6th root of 64 as 4 (treating 64 as 4^3) and then ran the incumbent's coordinate route flawlessly on the wrong ratio, producing a clean self-consistent circle. Critically it did spot-check points, but only against its own derived condition, so the check confirmed the error instead of catching it; several correct rollouts also burned tokens re-deriving individual roots. The revision therefore keeps the kept round-7 coordinate route and adds two portable guards: fix k by matching exponents and confirming k^n = |c| by multiplying out, and require any verification to return to the original equation rather than the derived modulus condition.

Training fell to 3/8 and the failure mode flipped from the containment error the incumbent was built to block: four of five failures now argue the overlap is ZERO (one committed the summed-areas answer outright, others derived disjointness from wrongly-signed edge inequalities or from a center-to-side distance exceeding the small shape's half-width), and the fifth burned the token cap on an unclosed tangency search. The incumbent only forbids overlap = all of S, giving no lower floor, so this revision adds the local argument that a corner at an interior point covers a positive-angle wedge of a surrounding set (so overlap cannot be zero or a single point) plus a cheap sign-orientation check for edge inequalities, which is the concrete step that produced the spurious disjointness.

My 8 public rollouts with the incumbent scored 7/8; the lone failure terminated normally, not by truncation, and it had already restated the partition advice before discarding it. It set P_k as the polynomial used for term k, so reuse was notationally impossible, then chained P_{k+1}(x_{k+1}) - P_k(x_k) = d, concluded consecutive polynomials differ by a constant hence each is usable once, and reported N. The revision keeps the incumbent's proven skeleton and adds the one missing notational rule - never index a function by the term index; a function owns a set of indices - and names the bijection trap that adjacent chaining creates.

Train fell to 3/8, and all five failures reduce to one mechanism applied at three different stages: reading log_{1/2} u = y as argument = 2^y instead of 2^{-y}. One botched the parameter fit that way, two botched the reduction factor (yielding a negative discriminant and an irrational quadratic, then thrashing to the length cap), and two reduced correctly but read a vertex's y with the sign flipped and reported an area from an off-graph point. The revision kills the direction trap at its source with the base identity plus an explicit large-argument-for-negative-y check, and adds the free degenerate-root test, which I confirmed evaluates to zero on the one correct reduction and to nonzero on both botched ones, so it catches exactly the failing traces before they burn their budget.

All 8 rollouts scored 0 and seven of them explicitly asserted the final order is a uniformly random permutation, then read the answers straight off that model (1/24 and 1/4); the eighth spent its whole budget on unstructured case work without committing. The incumbent already forbids symmetry claims in words, and rounds 1-8 show that adding more bans or structural facts only lengthened the hint and cost held-out, so this revision keeps the incumbent's pricing mechanism and swaps the passive ban for an active falsification step: enumerate the smallest instance by hand and check the uniform model against it before using it.

My 8 rollouts scored 4/8 and every success came from the ladder: solve n=2,3,4 by elimination, fit a signed reciprocal-factorial form, substitute the real size. The four failures split into one that skipped small cases entirely and guessed from a named 'moment theory' framing, two that abandoned a working ladder for a polynomial-coefficient framing and burned the token cap in self-contradiction loops, and one that had a fully verified closed form yet kept re-deriving until it hit the cap without emitting an answer. So this revision replaces the question-specific 'expect factorial growth' cue with a short menu of standard closed-form families (better transfer at lambda=5), adds an explicit stop-and-box trigger at first verified fit, and localizes any disagreement to the toy's arithmetic instead of a rebuild.

5/8 public rollouts were correct. Two failures showed the known substitution mode (took the stated group count as the unit count, saw every total divide evenly, and never invoked gcd), but the third failed differently and revealingly: it correctly enumerated candidate counts including the gcd, then in its own maximum-selection step named a smaller listed candidate as the maximum and answered from it. Since rounds 5-8 showed that adding more anti-substitution apparatus collapses heldout (0.2125 down to 0.1125/0.0625/0.125/0.1375), I kept the incumbent spine and ordering intact and spent the budget on the unused commute clause, replacing it with a portable selection discipline: compute the gcd by successive pairwise gcd instead of eyeballing a divisor list, and if candidates are enumerated, verify the kept one is a multiple of all others.

All 8 public rollouts were correct (8/8, 4.1k-9.1k tokens, none truncated), so the training question stays saturated and every remaining point is transfer. The one rollout that cost 9.1k tokens - roughly double the median - botched the composition step itself, substituting the outer coefficient into the wrong slot so it produced a lopsided relation whose exponents were not an A<->B swap, then spent thousands of tokens solving that corrupted relation, integer-guessing the center, and only recovered by accident. This revision keeps the proven trigger, centered ansatz, factored both-branch condition, parameter-count closure and symmetric-combination rule and adds only a portable composition rule (raise the inner offset, not the outer coefficient) plus a cheap swap-symmetry audit that catches a mis-raised exponent before any algebra is spent on it.

2/8 correct and all six failures ended at the 16384-token cap without committing an answer. The shared mechanical fault is the block swap: rollouts tracking an index through the sub-steps dropped or mis-shifted the earlier swaps (one wrote that an index stayed fixed under a swap that must move it, another effectively kept only the final sub-step), producing a composite of disjoint 2-cycles that contradicted their own state simulation, after which they thrashed between mutually inconsistent per-size counts. The revision states the exact +/-L offset-preserving shift and that it must be applied to the index currently held, and replaces the incumbent's open-ended redo instruction with reject-the-formula-not-the-simulation plus box-it-immediately so the budget is not burned.
